rationale: Prieto (2016) examines the tension between Chile's neoliberal water-rights privatization and market model under the 1981 Water Code and collective indigenous water ownership/customary communal governance (costumbres) among Atacameño communities in Chiu-Chiu and Lasana, making regulatory_model_ownership the dominant mechanism family (with CONADI water-fund purchase subsidies playing a supporting role as fees_tariffs_subsidies). The central empirical outcomes are institutional/governance outcomes (administrative_outcome): water-rights market transaction patterns (only 2 of 213 transactions to mining and 0 to urban utilities) and the recollectivization/decommodification of 58.3% of privatized water volume by indigenous communities while preventing external canal withdrawals. The study uses a mixed_methods design combining a quantitative census of Water Property Register transactions (1981-2009) with three field seasons of participant observation, oral histories, and semi-structured interviews.
